﴿within which are correct books﴾, meaning: within the purified scrolls are books from Allah, upright, just and straight, with no error in them, because they are from Allah.

.

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And Allah did not command these Jews and Christians, who are the People of the Book, except that they worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion; that is, devoting obedience solely to Him, not mixing their obedience to their Lord with shirk. The Jews associated partners with their Lord by saying that 'Uzayr is the son of Allah, and the Christians did likewise regarding the Messiah, and [both] denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿ḤUNAFĀʾ (inclining toward truth)﴾

Our explanation of the meaning of ḥanīfiyyah has already passed earlier, with its evidences sufficient to dispense with repeating it. However, we will mention some of the reports that we have not mentioned before concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

◦ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿sincere to Him in religion, inclining toward truth﴾, he said: pilgrims, Muslims, not polytheists; he said: and to establish prayer and give zakah, and to make pilgrimage, and that is the correct religion.

◦ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, inclining toward truth﴾; and ḥanīfiyyah is circumcision, and the prohibition of mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, and the rites of pilgrimage.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and to establish prayer and give zakah﴾

He says: and that they establish prayer, and that they give zakah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And that is the correct religion﴾

It means that what He mentioned He commanded these who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists is the correct religion. By "al-qayyimah" is meant the upright and just. The "religion" is attributed to "al-qayyimah," and religion is "al-qayyim," which is one of its attributes, the two words differing. In the reading of 'Abdullah, as far as I know, as was related to us: ﴿And that is the religion of the qayyimah﴾, and "qayyimah" is feminine because it is made an attribute of the religion (millah), as if it were said: and that is the upright millah, rather than Judaism and Christianity.

And the people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◦ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And that is the correct religion﴾: it is the religion which Allah sent His Messenger with, and legislated for Himself, and was pleased with.

◦ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Scriptures, upright﴾ and ﴿And that is the religion of the qayyimah﴾, he said: it is one; qayyimah: upright, moderate.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. They are the worst of creation" (6) "Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — it is they who are the best of creation" (7).

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), denying his prophethood, from among the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists, all of them, "in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein," meaning: remaining and dwelling therein "forever," not coming out of it and not dying therein. "They are the worst of creation," meaning: those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists are the worst of what God has created and brought into being. The Arabs do not hamz (pronounce the glottal stop in) the word al-bariyyah (creation), and the readers of the major cities recited it without hamz, except for something reported from Nafi' ibn Abi Nu'aym, for some of them related from him that he used to hamz it, taking it to the words of God, "before We bring it into being" (al-Hadid: 22), and that it is of the form fa'iliyyah derived from that. As for those who did not hamz it, their omission of the hamz in this has two possible explanations. The first is that they omitted the hamz in it as they omitted it in al-malak (the angel), which is of the form mif'al from alaka or la'aka, and in min yara (from one who sees), tara (you see), and nara (we see), which are of the form yaf'alu from ra'aytu (I saw). The second is that they took it to be of the form fa'iliyyah from al-bari, which means dust. It is related from the Arabs by hearing: "bi-fika al-bari" (into your mouth the dust), meaning by it: the dust.

* *

And His words: "Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — it is they who are the best of creation."

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messenger Muhammad, and worshipped God, sincere to Him in religion, upright (hunafa'), and established the prayer, and gave the zakah, and obeyed God in what He commanded and forbade, "it is they who are the best of creation," meaning: whoever does that among mankind, they are the best of creation. And indeed: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: 'Isa ibn Farqad related to us, from Abu al-Jarud, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, regarding "it is they who are the best of creation," that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You, O 'Ali, and your Shi'ah (followers)."

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is His majesty and sanctified are His names:** ﴿Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾ (98:8).

He, may He be exalted, says: The reward of those who believed and did righteous deeds, with their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, is ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, meaning gardens of lasting residence in which there is no departure. ﴿Rivers flow beneath their trees.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ means they remain there forever, not leaving them and not dying in them.

﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ for their obedience to Him in this world, and for their striving for deliverance from His punishment by it.

﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ for what He gives them of reward on that day, in return for their obedience to their Lord in this world, and for the honour He bestows upon them for it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: This good which I have described and promised to those who believed and did righteous deeds on the Day of Resurrection is for whoever fears his Lord. That is, for whoever feared Allah in this world, openly and secretly, so that he guarded himself by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. And success is from Allah.

End of the commentary on Surah Lam Yakun.
